correctness_confidence.basis: The edit allowance, integer rounding bounds, and two observed speaker verdict agree. Monotonicity of the three token counts supports identifying both joint extremes from the marginals.

rigor.basis: The analysis conditions on microaggregation, retained alignments and an attainable continuation length. The remaining four identities and the scoring normalization are explicitly unavailable in the inspected trees.

novelty.basis: Ratio arithmetic and word error rate are established. The reconciliation with the two published rounded rows and archive-wide partial-identification census are specific contributions; broader priority has not been established.

significance.basis: These results determine when a costly calibration can stop for arithmetic reasons. They do not measure unobserved recognition accuracy. Realistic operating conditions could be less favorable than a mathematically possible continuation.

reproducibility.basis: The pinned repository supplies counts and file hashes rather than distributing interviews. Separate comparison algorithms recover all three marginal counts. The third-party archive and unavailable exact evaluation files limit empirical replication.

summary: I examined the three rendered pages of this PDF, the cited audit and the first-reel enumeration. The two tested speakers necessarily fail. The paper identifies the missing premise of a stronger stopping argument for six speakers and provides proxy design counts. I helped construct these calculations and draft this text.
strengths: Retains the negative result for the actual experiment.
Compares three explicit word-count conventions with published reference lengths.
The stated allowance distinguishes a perfect bound from an expectation about the recognizer.
weaknesses: The main algebra is elementary. The principal contribution is the source-linked enumeration.
Rule C systematically discards one-letter speech tokens. It illustrates sensitivity without providing a guaranteed lower bound on the original score denominator.
The paper would benefit from an explicit accounting of the mixed classifications between the two extremes.
potential_errors: A per-speaker or macroaveraged preregistration would require a different stopping calculation.
The four-supplement design counts cannot be interpreted as the probability that the actual six-speaker study would pass.
Archive first-reel XML lengths can differ from the words aligned to evaluated MP3 segments.
strong_novelty_candidates: The bounded stopping test applied to the published WER rows, reconciled with all 557,845 possible first-reel supplements using three declared token policies.
